input.text: Wanshou Temple, the "Temple of Longevity," sits on the Long River — the waterway Ming and Qing emperors sailed between the Forbidden City and the Summer Palace. Built in fifteen seventy-seven, it became the imperial rest stop on that voyage: emperors would land here, burn incense, and take tea before continuing upstream to their gardens. That river link left it serene and graceful — pagoda, halls, gardens, and centuries of imperial gifts. Today it houses the Beijing Art Museum, its exhibits rotating through bronzes, paintings, porcelain, and Buddhist art from the city's collections; the courtyard gardens reward slow walkers year-round, and the old stage once rang with opera for imperial birthdays. Its neighborhood, Suzhou Street, ties into the river walk toward the Summer Palace — one quiet hour here, then the water onward: you'd be repeating the emperor's afternoon, at a fraction of the budget.
